rationale: bugs_open/343 P2, submitted as its own coherent task and making no causal claim. skipToNextLoopIteration persists the loop-skip advance with a SINGLE unretried repo.UpdateState, after skipToNextLoopIterationForAsync has already marked the failed awaited row terminal. So one optimistic-lock failure loses the advance AND the awaited-map delete, while the row is already terminal - which puts the reply's redelivery behind the processed_at duplicate guard (DUPLICATE_SKIPPED) and the continuation is gone for good. That is a lost continuation on exactly the error path that carried all 31 of 343's observed terminal outcomes. Every sibling advance on this coordinator already retries optimistic-lock failures - the park 10 attempts, handleCompleteResponse 15, the progress loop 5 - and the asymmetry is the whole of the defect. VERIFIED AS A PATH, UNVERIFIED AS EVER HAVING FIRED: this does not claim to be the wedge's mechanism and does not close 343. Fix: apply the mutations to a freshly loaded state inside a retry loop (the coordinator's own established shape, NOT UpdateStateWithRetry, whose reload discards caller mutations), and mark the row terminal only once that advance is durable.

plan.summary: Give the loop-skip advance the optimistic-lock retry discipline every other advance on this coordinator already has, and retire the awaited row only after that advance is durable. The mutations move into one applySkip closure applied to a freshly loaded state per attempt, so a reload cannot resurrect the resolved request or lose the advance; MarkAwaitedRequestComplete moves inside the loop, immediately after the UpdateState that succeeds, mirroring handleCompleteResponse's ordering.

edits.rationale: THE DEFECT. Replace the single unretried repo.UpdateState with a 10-attempt optimistic-lock retry loop that RELOADS and RE-APPLIES, using the same backoffWithJitter and IsOptimisticLockError shape as persistAwaitingStateWithRetry. The mutations are collected into one applySkip closure so the caller's copy and every retry attempt apply exactly the same changes and cannot drift. The error count is now read off the TARGET rather than the caller's copy, so a reload picks up a sibling's increment instead of overwriting it from a stale number. New skipToNextLoopIterationWithAwaited takes terminalRequestID and re-applies the awaited-map delete on every attempt; skipToNextLoopIteration forwards with an empty id so the synchronous caller (coordinator.go continue_on_error arm) is unchanged. DELIBERATELY NOT UpdateStateWithRetry: that helper recovers by reloading and doing *state = *reloaded, then re-issues the UPDATE with the reloaded, UNMUTATED state - the caller's mutations are silently discarded and a no-op is persisted. It is not a retrying version of 'save my changes', and a LANDMINES entry ships in this commit saying so.

ORDERING. The awaited row was marked terminal BEFORE the advance was persisted; when the persist then failed, the advance and the map delete were both lost while the row was already terminal, so the redelivery was eaten by the processed_at duplicate guard. The mark now happens inside the retry loop, immediately after the UpdateState that succeeds - the same rule handleCompleteResponse calls 'the key fix'. Inside the loop rather than after the function returns, because skipToNextLoopIteration ends by calling continueExecution: marking after that would hold the row open for the entire next iteration. A mark failure stays non-fatal (Warn) because the state is saved, which is the half a redelivery cannot recover. On the timeout path (retryExpiredAwaitedRequest) the row is already 'error' before entry, so that path's ordering is unchanged by construction.

Mutation-proven, and each mutation was APPLIED and its kill set recorded rather than assumed. M1 restore the single unretried write -> TestLoopSkipSurvivesAnOptimisticLockFailure fails (no second UPDATE, advance lost) and nothing else does. M2 move the mark back before the persist -> the two ordered-expectation tests fail, the awaited UPDATE arriving out of turn. M3 retire the row on the error return path too -> TestAwaitedRowIsNotRetiredWhenTheAdvanceDoesNotPersist fails and no other. The first draft of that test's comment named M2 as its killer and was WRONG - the claim survived a passing run, so it is corrected in the file. That test must also assert its negative POSITIVELY (expect the awaited UPDATE, require the expectation to remain UNMET), because MarkAwaitedRequestComplete's error is deliberately swallowed and a mock rejection is therefore invisible to the code under test.
edits.sketch:
new file, four tests:
  TestLoopSkipSurvivesAnOptimisticLockFailure  (lock failure -> reload -> re-apply -> UPDATE; asserts CurrentStep advanced, the resolved request did NOT come back from the reloaded row, and captured collected_data is non-empty)
  TestAwaitedRowIsNotRetiredWhenTheAdvanceDoesNotPersist  (non-lock error; the awaited expectation MUST remain unmet)
  TestLoopSkipCleanPathWritesOnceThenRetiresTheRow  (the control: one write, then the mark, in that order)
  TestSyncLoopSkipTouchesNoAwaitedRow  (empty terminalRequestID touches no awaited row at all)

grounded_in: loop_error_handler.go (pre-fix): 'repo := NewStateRepository(s.db, s.logger); if err := repo.UpdateState(ctx, state); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("failed to persist state after loop skip: %w", err) }' - one call, no optimistic-lock retry, on a path every sibling advance retries.

loop_error_handler.go skipToNextLoopIterationForAsync (pre-fix): MarkAwaitedRequestComplete runs FIRST, then delete(state.AwaitedRequests, requestID), then skipToNextLoopIteration - so the row is terminal before the advance is durable.

state.go UpdateStateWithRetry: '// Update our state reference with the reloaded version' followed by '*state = *reloaded' then 'continue' - the retried UPDATE carries the reloaded, unmutated state, which is why this fix cannot use it.
coordinator.go handleCompleteResponse, the ordering this now mirrors: 'SUCCESS - NOW mark the awaited request as complete. This is the key fix: only mark complete AFTER state is saved.'

coordinator.go DUPLICATE_SKIPPED, keyed on processed_at - the guard that eats a redelivery once the row has been marked terminal, which is what makes a lost advance unrecoverable rather than merely retried.

The retry disciplines this one lacked, for comparison: persistAwaitingStateWithRetry maxRetries := 10; handleCompleteResponse maxRetries := 15; handleProgressUpdate maxRetries := 5 - all with backoffWithJitter and IsOptimisticLockError.

Owner ruling 2026-07-29 section 1: an addition needs an RFC only when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES. Restoring 'an advance persists with the same retry discipline as every other advance' repairs a stated guarantee; it adds no field, no new authority, and no default-path behaviour change.
plan.risks: (1) THE ORDERING CHANGE IS THE ONE TO CHECK: the awaited row is now retired later than before. Between the successful persist and the mark, a redelivery could in principle be claimed and drive the step again - but the state is already advanced past it at that point, so the duplicate arrives for a step that is no longer current, which is the same window handleCompleteResponse has always had. The reverse ordering is what loses work outright, so this trades a narrow pre-existing window for an unrecoverable loss. (2) The mark now sits INSIDE the retry loop rather than after continueExecution; a reviewer should confirm that placement, since marking after the function returns would hold the row open for the whole next iteration. (3) The error count is now derived from the reloaded state rather than the caller's copy - intentional (it stops a stale copy overwriting a sibling's increment) but it is a behaviour change under contention and should be read as one. (4) *state = *freshState adopts the reloaded copy wholesale, because the caller goes on to build a continuation context from that pointer and it must describe the row actually written; a reviewer should check no caller depends on fields of the pre-reload copy. (5) WHAT THIS IS NOT: verified as a path, unverified as ever having fired. It does not close bugs_open/343 and no comment, commit message or register entry says it explains the wedge. If a wedge recurs after this rolls, that is signal that the mechanism is elsewhere - RSH-011's capture stays armed, with its trigger deliberately broad.
